chief_complaint: atypical sharp chest pain lasting a few seconds, unrelated to exertion
hpi_details: A 65-year-old male presents to the clinic with atypical sharp chest pain lasting a few seconds, unrelated to exertion. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks he strained a muscle between his ribs while raking leaves in the yard or that it is sharp trapped gas from indigestion.
concerns: He is worried that this sudden chest pain is a warning sign of a fatal heart attack like the one that killed his father at age sixty-five.
expectations: He hopes to get an ECG done today and reassurance from the doctor that his heart is completely healthy.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Costochondritis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.

Standard management emphasizes Plan for Costochondritis: Perform chest wall palpation, obtain ECG to rule out cardiac, recommend NSAIDs, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

teaching.one_liner: Inflammation where rib meets sternum. The pain is sharp, positional, and — the key finding — reproduced by pressing on the spot.
red_flags: Do not settle on this until cardiac and pulmonary causes are genuinely excluded

must_ask.say: Does it hurt more if you press on that spot?
Does moving your arm or taking a deep breath make it worse?
How long does each episode last — seconds, or much longer?
Have you done any heavy lifting, new exercise, or had a bad cough?
Does it ever come on with exertion, or with sweating and nausea?
What are you most worried this might be?

history.answer: I've been getting these brief, sharp stabbing pains in my chest that last just a couple of seconds at a time.
It started about four or five days ago while I was just relaxing at home, and it has been slowly happening more often.
It's on the left side of my chest, just to the left of the breastbone, and I can point right to the spot with one finger.
It feels like a sharp needle poke or a sudden jab, not a pressure or tight ache.
No, it stays right in that one spot on my chest and doesn't spread to my arm, neck, jaw, or back.
Each sharp jab lasts only two to three seconds, but it happens several times throughout the day.
When the jab hits, it is about a 6 out of 10, but it goes away completely once the second passes.
Walking or climbing stairs doesn't bring it on, and it can happen whether I'm sitting down or walking around.
Taking a very deep breath or twisting my upper body sometimes triggers a quick jab, and pressing on the spot definitely hurts.
No, eating doesn't change it at all, and I haven't had any sour fluid coming up, heartburn, or trouble swallowing.
No, I haven't had any cold sweats, shortness of breath, nausea, or lightheadedness when it happens.
No fever, no chills, and no cough or phlegm.
I have been feeling more tired and worn out than usual over the past week, even though I've been resting.
About a week before this started, I had a mild head cold with a runny nose, but that cleared up.
No, neither leg is swollen or sore, and I haven't been on any long flights or had surgery recently.
No, I checked my skin in the mirror and there are no bumps, blisters, or rashes anywhere on my chest.
No, I haven't had racing heartbeat attacks, numbness in my hands, or feelings of sudden terror.
Over the weekend before the pain started, I was doing some heavy yard work and moving bags of soil, which was more lifting than I usually do.
No, I have never had chest pain like this before, and I've never needed heart tests or stents.
I don't have high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol as far as my regular checkups have shown.
I thought maybe I pulled a muscle between my ribs raking the yard, or that it's just sharp trapped gas from indigestion.
My father died suddenly of a heart attack when he was sixty-five, so every sharp pain makes me terrified I'm about to have one too.
I've generally been healthy and don't have any chronic medical illnesses.
I had an appendectomy when I was in my twenties, but nothing else since then.
I don't take any prescription drugs, just a daily multivitamin.
No allergies to medications or anything else that I know of.
I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only have a glass of beer once or twice a month at social gatherings.
I'm retired from administrative office work and live quietly at home with my wife.
No one in my family had early heart attacks or sudden heart disease; both of my parents lived into their eighties.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 99% on room air, temperature 36.6°C.
Alert, comfortable at rest, not in acute distress, no pallor or diaphoresis.
No jugular venous distension, normal jugular venous pulsations visible without elevation.
Marked tenderness and exact reproduction of sharp pain on direct palpation over the left 3rd and 4th costochondral junctions, without swelling or warmth.
Resonant percussion notes bilaterally and symmetrically across all lung fields.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally without wheezing, crackles, or pleural friction rubs.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2, no murmurs, gallops, or pericardial friction rubs.
Soft, non-tender across all quadrants, no epigastric tenderness, and no organomegaly.
No erythematous rash, vesicles, or dermatomal lesions across the anterior or posterior chest wall.
No pretibial or ankle edema bilaterally.
Calves are soft, non-tender, symmetric in circumference, with no cords or localized warmth.
